mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates and boosts valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) below 520,000 million dollars and housing starts (HOUST) below 1,600 thousand units indicate broad-based demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both RSAFS < 520000 and HOUST < 1600, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates monetary tightening that suppresses corporate investment and consumer spending, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 108.0 indicates manufacturing and services contraction that reduces corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 108.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that supports strong consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) below 152,000 thousand persons signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is below 152000, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production (INDPRO) decline below 108.0 indicates supply chain disruption that reduces corporate margins and consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 108.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
